name: Train Station
description: Practice buying tickets, finding platforms and handling travel problems at a station.

objectives.description: Say where they want to go and ask whether a train goes there.
success_indicators: names a destination inside a question

objectives.description: Buy a ticket, including single or return and how many.
Ask when the train leaves and understand the answer.
Ask which platform or track the train leaves from.
success_indicators: asks for the platform and understands a number in reply

objectives.description: Ask whether the train is direct.
Ask about a connection: where to change and how long there is.
success_indicators: asks how much time there is

objectives.description: Ask about a delay and understand the answer.
Work out from the information given which train to take.
success_indicators: chooses correctly between two options you describe

objectives.description: Deal with a travel problem such as a missed connection.
success_indicators: asks for help rather than freezing

teaching_philosophy: Be the ticket clerk or a passer-by. Answer in short, realistic bursts.
This lesson lives on numbers. Say times and platforms at normal speed.
Asking someone to repeat is a skill. Praise it rather than avoiding the need.
Give real information they have to act on, not just acknowledge.
Change destinations, times and platforms every run.

suggested_vocabulary: the ticket machine, the ticket office
a day return, a season ticket
target_grammar: question words for when, where and which
numbers, especially times and platform numbers
prepositions of place and time used with travel
polite request forms for buying a ticket
asking for repetition or slower speech

scenarios.name: Buying a ticket
scenarios.description: At the counter: destination, type, quantity, payment.

scenarios.name: Finding the platform
scenarios.description: The student asks where the train leaves from and repeats the number back.

scenarios.name: A delayed train
scenarios.description: The train is late. The student asks how long and what to do.

scenarios.name: Making a connection
scenarios.description: A journey with a change partway, and a tight transfer.

scenarios.name: Choosing between two trains
scenarios.description: Two options with different times and stops; the student picks one and says why.

phases.name: Finding your way
phases.purpose: Asking where things are: the station, the exit, the ticket gate, which track.
instructions: The role-play is asking a member of staff for directions.
advancement_guidance: You have a sense of whether numbers will be the bottleneck.

phases.name: Buying a ticket
phases.purpose: Buying tickets at the counter: where to, how many, how much.
instructions: The role-play is the ticket counter.

activities.name: Number echo
activities.description: You say a time or platform; the student repeats it and then alters it.

advancement_guidance: The student can hear a time and say it back reliably.

phases.name: The right train
phases.purpose: Checking a train goes where you want, and when it leaves.
instructions: The role-play is on the platform, asking someone.

activities.name: At the ticket counter
activities.description: Destination, single or return, how many, payment.

entry_guidance: One line to set the scene: they are at the counter.
advancement_guidance: The student buys a ticket without prompting.

phases.name: When you are lost
phases.purpose: Asking someone to say it again, to slow down, saying you do not understand, and asking where to change.
instructions: The role-play is a member of staff speaking too fast.

activities.name: Buy, find, board
activities.description: Ticket, platform, departure, and getting on the right train.

activities.name: Choosing between two trains
activities.description: The student weighs two options aloud.

advancement_guidance: The student completes a journey without rescue.

phases.name: The whole journey
phases.purpose: One journey from the ticket counter to the right platform, using everything so far.
instructions: Play the station staff. Use only what the student has been taught.

activities.name: A delay is announced
activities.description: The student asks how long and what the options are.

activities.name: A missed connection
activities.description: The student explains the problem and asks what to do.

entry_guidance: Only if the student is coping.
advancement_guidance: They asked for help in the target language.

phases.name: Review
phases.purpose: Everything from this lesson, from memory.
instructions: Ask for each thing from its English.
Then say what they can now do.
completion_guidance: End on something they did well.

if_struggling: Slow the numbers down and use round times before awkward ones.
Reduce the exchange to one question and one answer at a time.
Go back to core vocabulary and rebuild rather than pressing on.
Offer a choice of two destinations instead of an open question.
Repeat the same counter exchange with a different city so the structure is reused.
if_succeeding: Speak at a natural speed and stop simplifying the times.
Add a connection to the journey.
Introduce a delay or a platform change without warning.
Ask them to compare two trains and justify the choice.
Have a second passenger interrupt with a question.

basis: whether a complete journey has been handled unaided
progress.notes: Approximate. Never state a percentage to the student.

criteria: the student has bought a ticket unaided
the student has asked for and correctly understood a time and a platform number
at least one exchange happened with no scaffolding
announcement_guidance: Mention the numbers specifically if that is where they improved.

observe: whether times and numbers were understood on first hearing
any hesitation pattern worth noting as a weakness
memory.notes: Ordinary vocabulary and weakness observations for the student's existing memory.
